teaser.text: Bank of America is a financial-services company that sells access to money, credit, investment help and financial tools for businesses and investors. Its business becomes clear when you follow a dollar: a customer supplies funds or pays a fee, the bank puts that money to work, pays the costs of its promises and keeps what remains.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Bank of America’s base, bear and bull cases?

paragraphs.text: The base case carries 50% probability. Bear and bull cases carry 30% and 20%, respectively. Q4 2026 tests whether the NII outlook holds and operating leverage turns positive; weaker asset repricing or higher deposit costs would pressure the case. The scheduled surcharge increase on January 1, 2027 could constrain buybacks. The stress capital buffer—extra capital required by stress tests—is fixed through September 30, 2027. Sustained wealth flows, improving efficiency and technology productivity support the base or bull cases; persistent compliance costs or weaker credit shift the outlook toward the bear case.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Bank of America really make?

paragraphs.text: The gap is not an immediate cash bill if BAC holds the securities until repayment. But selling under pressure would crystallize the discount, while holding the assets leaves money tied up at older yields. Operating cash flow also cannot be treated as cash available to shareholders, because loans, securities, collateral and compliance continue to absorb funds.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Bank of America today?

paragraphs.text: Bank of America’s stock price is a bet on what its capital can earn in the future. At $51.39 on October 15, 2026, the market is asking whether a recent setback is temporary and whether the bank can keep producing returns strong enough to justify paying above tangible book.

A P/E ratio says how much investors pay for each dollar of earnings, not how quickly an investment will be recovered. The trailing multiple implies about $4.21 of recent earnings per share. The forward multiple implies about $4.55, so it looks cheaper only because analysts expect earnings to recover; that forecast can be wrong.

blocks.heading: How much does Bank of America pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The board authorized $40 billion of additional repurchases in 2025, while the quarterly dividend rose to $0.32 in 2026. An authorization is permission, not a promise to spend. In the third quarter of 2026, Bank of America reported 10.9 percent CET1 capital against a 10 percent minimum, leaving limited room above the regulatory floor.

blocks.heading: Does Bank of America’s dividend have earnings coverage?

paragraphs.text: The healthier decision came after earnings improved: return money only after rebuilding the cushion. In 2025, earnings for common shareholders were $29,055 million, against $8,083 million of dividends and $21,433 million of buybacks. The share count fell from 8,558.4 million in 2021 to 7,680.9 million in 2025, so profits were divided among fewer shares. But distributions exceeded 2025 earnings, which cannot continue indefinitely without reducing capital.

blocks.heading: What could change Bank of America’s dividend?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise gradually in the base case from $1.36 per share to $1.44 and then $1.52. The first figure is close to the 30% payout applied to forward earnings. The bear case holds at $1.28 before falling to $1.20, while the bull case rises from $1.40 to $1.56 and then $1.72. The bear path reflects the 10.9% CET1 ratio and higher capital demands; the bull path assumes stronger earnings absorb them.

The January 1, 2027 surcharge increase would push the forecast toward the bear case if it limits buybacks or delays dividend growth. Conversely, capital generation that preserves distributions would support the base case.

earnings.opening: Bank of America’s next results are expected on January 15, 2027. Bank of America’s key watch is whether earnings growth survives higher compliance costs and tighter capital requirements.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Bank of America makes money, who its rivals are, how its management works, and what risks it faces.

blocks.heading: What has Bank of America guided for?

paragraphs.text: Bank of America reaffirmed full-year NII growth near the top of its 6.0%–8.0% range and introduced an expectation of at least 8% growth in 2027. Its destination is 12.0% EPS growth and a 16.0%–18.0% return on tangible common equity. Buybacks can lift EPS and that return by reducing the number of shares and the equity base, so investors must separate operating improvement from denominator management. Compliance costs will test that distinction.

blocks.heading: Has Bank of America kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: There is also a completed test: the 2023 performance units paid 100% after their performance period ended in 2025. The rules did not remove litigation, fines or penalties from the calculation, which matters because shareholders bear those costs.

blocks.heading: What does Bank of America’s recent revenue and profit trend show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose across 2021–2025, driven mainly by net interest income. But that income dipped in 2024 before recovering. Loan balances, deposit pricing, market rates and the replacement of older assets with higher-yielding ones all matter. Investment and brokerage income also benefited from stronger markets and new client assets, which are different from growth caused by larger loan balances.

Profit tells a weaker story. Net income in 2025 was below its 2021 level because 2021 benefited from a large credit-loss release, while 2025 absorbed substantial provisions. EPS nevertheless rose because fewer shares divided the result. If fewer people share the same pot, each remaining person receives more; that does not make the pot larger.
